factual_errors: Section 9 is internally inconsistent about scope: it says 'three existing files modified' while simultaneously requiring changes to Build SKILL.md, Review SKILL.md, the four agent frontmatter files (kept pin-free), the existing frontmatter test, and new prose-contract tests — that is more than three files.

Section 7 enumerates FALLBACK_TO_MAIN 'when inheritance is guaranteed' and FALLBACK_TO_HOST_DEFAULT 'when inheritance is not guaranteed', but Section 2 defines guarantees_parent_inheritance as a three-valued field including 'unknown'. The 'unknown' case has no defined outcome mapping.

Section 10's claim that the policy 'would authorize none of six historical direct-high dispatches' cannot follow from the stated evidence, because Section 5's final high trigger ('the main agent already uses high') depends on main-profile data the packet says was not retained. The claim is unsupported as written, not merely uncertain.
Section 4 example table is presented as covering the rules but omits every non-low, non-high main effort (e.g. frontier/medium, standard/medium), which is exactly where rules 3 and 4 collide.
judgment_calls: Model-first-then-effort ordering for complex work is a reasonable but unvalidated cost heuristic; no evidence is offered that a stronger model at unchanged effort dominates the reverse ordering.
Making 'insufficient-evidence' the highest-precedence class (execute at main 0/0) is a defensible conservatism choice, not a correctness requirement.
Refusing a persistent dispatch ledger and keeping the record in active task context is a maintainability judgment; it does cost cross-session learning.
Mechanical work applying both model -1 and effort -1 is a policy preference, not derivable from the stated principles.
Excluding role and round names as classification inputs is a judgment call that discards real, if weak, signal.
contradictions_or_non_executable_transit: Section 4 rule 3 vs rule 4: for a main profile of frontier/medium, a complex task 'may raise effort by one step' (→ high) while rule 4 forbids a non-high main profile from becoming high on initial dispatch and clamps to medium. The transition is undefined/self-cancelling for that input.

Section 3 precedence 'insufficient-evidence > complex' vs Section 5 step 1: a complex task with a missing acceptance condition is classified insufficient-evidence and executed at 0/0, yet the escalation ladder assumes the packet defect is repaired and retried at the same profile — the two paths are not reconciled and no rule says when a repaired packet is reclassified.

Section 2's 'omit both overrides and record host-default/unverified' when the main profile is unobservable produces an effective_profile with no matching outcome in Section 7: no fallback was triggered, so neither ROUTED nor either FALLBACK_* value is accurate.

Section 5 step 3 caps escalated effort at medium 'initially', while step 4 lists high triggers; the ordering between a step-3 medium result and a subsequently observable step-4 trigger is unspecified, so 'escalate one cause at a time' has no defined successor state.

Section 8's record has a single scalar escalation_reason and outcome, which cannot represent the multi-attempt escalation ladder of Section 5 (repair-retry, then model raise, then effort raise) within one dispatch.
false_downgrade_risks: Mechanical class applies model -1 and effort -1 simultaneously — a two-step downgrade that contradicts the proposal's own one-change-at-a-time discipline and can drop a standard/low baseline to economy/low on edits whose 'mechanical verification' is weaker than assumed.
'Exact targets plus mechanical verification' is satisfiable by a passing-but-shallow test suite, so genuinely subtle refactors classify as mechanical.
insufficient-evidence forcing 0/0 means the hardest, least-specified tasks — the ones most likely to need a stronger model — are systematically denied any upgrade.
'Crossing multiple files alone is not complex' plus the ban on role/round signals leaves broad-refactor work defaulting to ordinary.
Fallback to omitted overrides silently downgrades an intended frontier dispatch to host default with no retry at an intermediate tier.
false_upgrade_risks: The complex class list — 'design trade-off' and 'evidence conflict' in particular — matches nearly any non-trivial review or planning packet, so complex becomes the default and model +1 is applied routinely.
'Irreversible architecture' has no observable test; a self-describing packet can assert it.
Section 5 step 4's 'the same blocker survived a substantive fix' does not require the fix to have been competent, so a bad first attempt buys high effort.
Inheriting a main-agent high into every ordinary subagent (rule 5) upgrades all ordinary work whenever the user sets a high baseline, defeating the cost objective the policy exists to serve.
'medium could not settle a high-risk decision' relies on self-assessment by the agent that just failed, which is a weak gate.
structured_output.fallback_assessment: "Largely yes, with one gap. The routing path in Section 6 is fully mechanical — one retry with both overrides omitted, then a terminal state — and never solicits a model, effort, retry, or fallback choice from the user. Two caveats: (a) EXECUTION_FAILED and REQUIREMENT_BLOCKED are terminal and will surface to the user, but neither asks for a routing decision, so the claim holds; (b) the 'unknown' value of guarantees_parent_inheritance has no defined outcome mapping, and unless a default is written down an implementer will plausibly resolve it by asking. Fix the unknown-inheritance default and the no-user-decision property is genuinely closed."
smallest_required_changes: Resolve the rule 3 / rule 4 collision explicitly: state that rule 4's clamp is absolute and rule 3 applies only when main effort is low, then extend the example table with a frontier/medium and a standard/medium main row.
Map guarantees_parent_inheritance: unknown to FALLBACK_TO_HOST_DEFAULT explicitly.
Add an outcome value (or reuse FALLBACK_TO_HOST_DEFAULT with fallback_triggered: false) for the Section 2 unobservable-main-profile path so every terminal state has exactly one enum member.

Define the reclassification rule after a Section 5 step-1 packet repair: state that the repaired packet is re-classified, and that insufficient-evidence precedence applies only to the pre-repair attempt.
Make escalation_reason and outcome in Section 8 a list of per-attempt entries so the escalation ladder is representable.
Change mechanical to a single-step adjustment (model -1, effort unchanged, except the explicit frontier/high → standard/medium case) to match the proposal's own one-change-at-a-time principle.
Add one observable disambiguator for 'design trade-off' and 'evidence conflict' so complex is not the default class.
delete_instead_of_expand: The '100–145 maintained lines' estimate in Section 9 — it is unverifiable, the proposal already says it must be replaced by real diff counts, and the accompanying 'three existing files' count is wrong.

The six-historical-dispatches result in Section 10 — the text concedes in the same paragraph that it proves nothing, and its premise depends on main-profile data that was not retained. Keep only the sentence stating that no reduction is claimed.
The 'Rejected options' entry for 'Simultaneously raising model and effort' — it is restated normatively as the model-first rule in Section 4 and adds nothing as a separate rejection.
The prose gloss 'Ordinary Build and Review verification still judges the work product' in Section 6 — it is not a routing rule and blurs the fallback contract.
